title: Typical length-matching tolerances
note: Typical starting points from vendor documents; the SoC/PHY design guide for your part always wins. Times convert to length with TI's rule of thumb 1 ps = 5 mil (0.127 mm) for stripline; microstrip is about 10% faster (TI divides microstrip length by 1.1). Values were read from the cited documents on the date given; a field is null where no source could be read or confirmed, with the reason in notes.

rows.notes: SNLA387 says the MDI traces should be length-matched within 20 mil for 1G (it does not say within or between pairs), total length under 2 in. Between-pair figures quoted elsewhere (TI E2E answers on DP83867E/DP83869HM: 250 mil maximum, ideally 20 mil; NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX/Nano design guide DG-10931: about 0.22-0.25 mm) could not be read to confirm (E2E returned 403; the NVIDIA guide needs a developer login).

source.doc: TI SNLA387, Ethernet PHY PCB Design Layout Checklist (June 2021)

rows.notes: SNLA387: MDI traces length-matched within 50 mil for 100M or 10M; under 2 in.

source.doc: TI SNLA387, Ethernet PHY PCB Design Layout Checklist (June 2021)

rows.notes: SNLA387: MII traces length-matched within 20 mil for 1G, 50 mil for 100M/10M; RX traces to the other RX traces and TX to TX; under 6 in. Renesas R01AN6272EJ0141 (RZ/G, Rev. 1.41): RXC, RD[3:0] and RX_CTL the same length (clock not shorter), likewise TXC, TD[3:0], TX_CTL; the clock delay comes from RGMII-ID (receiver skew 1.0-2.6 ns), not from PCB length.

source.doc: TI SNLA387 (June 2021); Renesas R01AN6272EJ0141 Rev. 1.41, PCB Design Guideline for RGMII Interface

rows.notes: Row 'Skew within any USB3/PCIe/SGMII differential pair'. TX and RX pairs need not match each other (SPRAAR7 2.3).

source.doc: TI SPRAAR7J, High-Speed Interface Layout Guidelines (Feb 2023)

rows.notes: Same 50 mil in Tables A-1, A-3, A-4, A-7, A-8; trace length 4000-12000 mil depending on SoC.

source.doc: TI SPRAAR7J, High-Speed Interface Layout Guidelines (Feb 2023)

rows.notes: TX and RX pairs need not match each other; match intra-pair at the mismatched end (SPRAAR7 2.3).

source.doc: TI SPRAAR7J, High-Speed Interface Layout Guidelines (Feb 2023)

rows.interface: PCIe (Gen 1-3 as in the TI tables)

between_pairs.value: 550 mil total between all RX pairs, and between all TX pairs (KeyStone II); RX 6 ns / TX 1.5 ns (AM65x/AM64x)

rows.notes: Lane-to-lane allowances differ a lot by SoC: use the one for your part. mm is the 550 mil figure.

source.doc: TI SPRAAR7J, High-Speed Interface Layout Guidelines (Feb 2023)
source.section: Tables A-3, A-4 (550 mil); A-5, A-6 (ns)

rows.notes: TX and RX pairs need not match each other.

source.doc: TI SPRAAR7J, High-Speed Interface Layout Guidelines (Feb 2023)

rows.notes: From the row 'Skew within any USB3/SATA/PCIe/HDMI differential pair' of Table A-2 (AM57xx); that table's text extracts with jumbled columns, so read it on the page before relying on it. Between-pair figures (e.g. Intel AN 952) were not confirmed.

source.doc: TI SPRAAR7J, High-Speed Interface Layout Guidelines (Feb 2023)

rows.impedance: 100 ohm differential (85-115), loosely coupled; 50 ohm single-ended

within_pair.value: must meet the D-PHY mode-conversion limits; general estimate UI/50 (8 ps at UI 400 ps)

between_pairs.value: lane skew 40 ps = 0.1 UI at 1.25 GHz

rows.notes: Loosely coupled because D-PHY also signals single-ended at low power. mm values use 1 ps = 0.127 mm at UI 400 ps; scale with your UI. DSI uses the same D-PHY, but this source covers CSI.

source.doc: TI SPRAAR7J, High-Speed Interface Layout Guidelines (Feb 2023)

rows.impedance: set by the SoC guide's impedance table (Table 1-1)

within_pair.value: CK P/N 0.4 ps per segment, 0.8 ps total; DQS P/N 0.4 ps

between_pairs.value: DQS to DQ within a byte 2 ps; ADDR_CTRL to CK 3 ps per segment, 4 ps total; byte length up to 500 ps; byte-to-byte matching neither required nor recommended

rows.notes: Lengths in ps are stripline-equivalent (1 ps = 5 mil; microstrip / 1.1). mm values: 0.4 ps and 2 ps.

source.doc: TI SPRAD06C, AM62x, AM62Lx DDR Board Design and Layout Guidelines (rev. March 2025)

rows.impedance: set by the SoC guide's impedance table (Table 1-1)

within_pair.value: CK P/N 0.75 ps; DQS P/N 1.5 ps

between_pairs.value: DQS to its byte 150 ps; ADDR_CTRL to CK +-312.5 ps; CK longer than each DQS by 0-3 tCK; a DQ at most 49 ps shorter than its DQS

rows.notes: Per-bit deskew in the PHY loosens these; a PHY without it needs far tighter matching. mm values: 0.75 ps and 150 ps.

source.doc: TI SPRAD06C, AM62x, AM62Lx DDR Board Design and Layout Guidelines (rev. March 2025)

rows.notes: Not confirmed: the Intel EMIF length-matching page cited (ADDR/CMD to CK +-20 ps) no longer exists. Use your SoC's DDR3 guide.

rows.interface: eMMC / SD (HS200), QSPI/OSPI, LVDS / FPD-Link, DisplayPort / eDP, HDMI 2.1 FRL, USB4, MIPI C-PHY, DDR5, 2.5G-10GBASE-T
rows.notes: No primary source read yet; secondary figures (e.g. eMMC CLK to CMD/DAT 250 mil, DisplayPort intra 5 mil, HDMI 2.1 intra 3 mil, 10GBASE-T intra 5 mil) are left out until checked against a vendor guide.
